cohort_total_n_excerpt: A total of 142 matched pairs of subjects were investigated in this study.
reason: The study evaluates prostate cancer occurrence overall. It does not report an aggressive, advanced, high-grade, metastatic, or lethal incident prostate cancer endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: An increased risk of prostate cancer development was observed with the early first spermatorrhea (age < 18) (OR = 2.90, 95% CI: 1.76 - 4.80), early first sexual intercourse (age < or = 24) (OR = 2.38, 95% CI: 1.14 - 4.96), frequent sexual intercourse before 35 year old (OR = 1.80, 95% CI: 1.19 - 2.70), family history of cancer (OR = 2.70, 95% CI: 1.31 - 5.58), more intake of pork (OR =2.27, 95% CI: 1.38 - 3.70).
estimate_classifications.reason: The pork estimate concerns overall prostate cancer development, with no aggressive disease restriction.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Factors in lowing the risks were the fruit intake and drinking of green tea by OR value at 0.25 (95% CI: 0.08 - 0.75) and 0.52 (95% CI: 0.28 -0.96) respectively.
estimate_classifications.reason: The green-tea estimate concerns overall prostate cancer risk and is not restricted to aggressive disease.
